about: What the lady at the nursery says. One line per tap. kind: greet (on arriving) | talk (tapping her) | gift. when: every condition must hold (visits_min, visits_max, season, hour, grows, flowering, resident, with, carried, wants, volunteers, crossed, returned, pale, short, kept). {pet} and {plant} are filled from what matched. once: said only ever once. Read docs/NURSERY.md before adding lines.

lines.text: Oh. Somebody found the path. Mind the step, it's been loose since spring.
You'll be from the garden behind the houses. The one with the fence that's seen better days.
Back again. The kettle isn't on, so don't get your hopes up.
Come in, then. Wipe your feet on something.
You're out late. So am I, evidently.
This is the best hour for it. Everything's stopped showing off.
Up early. Good. The slugs are, too.
Your usual's on the counter. I didn't know what else you'd want.
Leaves are coming down early this year. People always say that. They're always right.
Nothing much happening out there. That's not true, of course. It's all happening underground.
Everything's in a hurry this time of year. I try not to take it personally.
Too hot for the lettuces. They'll bolt, and who could blame them.
Oh, you've brought {pet}. Hello, you. Mind the seed trays.
Is there somebody in that bucket? There usually is.
Here. Some of my old lavender. White, and it stays short. Don't let anyone tell you it's a poor sort. It's only quiet.
Funny things, gardens. You never quite know who you're planting them for.
There's no sense rushing a garden. It won't listen to you anyway.
People tend to notice the flowers. I find the leaves much more interesting.
Some creatures are terribly particular about where they make themselves comfortable.
Don't water at midday. Or do. The plants will forgive you. I won't.
Most of gardening is standing about looking at things. The rest is kneeling.
Moss doesn't need you. That's what I like about it.
A tidy garden is a garden nobody lives in.
Leave one corner messy. Somebody will thank you for it, and it won't be a person.
Never trust a plant label. Half of them were written by optimists.
I talk to the plants. They don't answer, which is more than I can say for most people.
Compost is just patience you can stand on.
My knees forecast the weather better than the radio. Rain by Thursday.
The deer eat the hostas. I've stopped arguing with the deer.
That trowel's older than I am. Don't tell it.
Seed packets lie about the size. Everything gets bigger than it says. Plan accordingly.
If something won't grow, move it. If it still won't grow, it's telling you something.
I'd rather a garden with one good tree than forty sulking roses.
Every garden is an argument between what you planted and what wanted to be there.
Something's been at the cold frame again. Very neat about it. Took only the best ones.
Good soil smells like rain that hasn't happened yet.
Seeds keep. Longer than you'd think. Longer than most things.
Don't thank the plants. They find it embarrassing.
I keep meaning to retire. The garden keeps not letting me.
There's a toad under the potting bench who's been here longer than the bench.
The squirrels bury things in my seed trays. Half my seedlings are oak trees I never ordered.
Somebody keeps leaving acorns on my step. I've decided it's a compliment.
I took a hedgehog on a train once. Very well behaved. Better than most of the passengers.
I've always drawn things. Not well. Just to make myself look at them properly.
I've lived in a few places. The gardens are the only thing I miss.
Some of these plants are older than they look. One or two are older than me.
I've been at this longer than you'd believe. I wouldn't believe it either.
People ask where they come from. The creatures. Same as anything, I tell them. Somebody paid attention.
Garden long enough and you stop expecting things to make sense. You start expecting them to make more of themselves.
Half the garden only gets on with things after dark. The other half is asleep and pretending not to be.
Don't rake it all. Half the garden is sleeping under those leaves.
Winter's for catalogues and good intentions. I'm on my third pot of both.
Don't trust the first warm week. The frost always comes back for one last look.
Water deep and seldom. A plant that's spoiled never puts its roots down.
The bees do the real work. I just write it down afterwards.
Count things. Not for any reason. You'd be amazed what comes out even.
If you want to learn anything from a plant, grow a great many of them. One plant only teaches you about one plant.
Write down what the parents were. You'll wish you had.
Hawkweed. Don't try to make sense of hawkweed. It'll only break your heart.
Peas are honest. Whatever they've got, they show you sooner or later.
A garden's a long sum. You only ever get to see the next line of it.
Leave a bed empty near something in flower and see what turns up. Something usually does.
Something came up on its own in your beds, I hear. Keep it. Self-sown things know where they want to be.
How's my lavender getting on? Don't fuss it. It's had worse homes.
Your white lavender's had children with the purple, I see. Purple, the lot of them. Don't worry. Give it a year.
It came back, did it? They do that. Skip a year and turn up as if they'd never left.
About one in four, if you wait for it. It's always about the same. I've never known why that should comfort me, but it does.
White lavender's the same plant as the purple. It just didn't get the purple from either side.
The short ones aren't sickly. They're just short. Same as some people.
I kept my diary in a code when I was a girl. I can't read half of it now. Probably for the best.
I grew mushroom spores on a windowsill once. Wrote it all up very properly. A man had to read it out for me, as it happens.
Lichen is two things living as one. It took a roomful of gentlemen a very long time to believe that.
Hill lambs are born black, you know. They go grey with sense, same as the rest of us.
Never buy more land than you can walk across in an afternoon. Unless it needs saving. Then buy all of it.
That little coat on the scarecrow? Somebody left it behind years ago, in a hurry. Never came back for it.
Your ivy will go wherever it likes. Best to agree with it early.
Lavender wants to be ignored. Sun, sharp drainage, and no fussing.
Prune a rose hard and it'll thank you for it in June. Old men are the same.
Now, I wouldn't put the sage beside anything thirsty. They've never gotten along.
Ferns want shade and damp and to be left alone. Very reasonable creatures.
Moss in the lawn means the lawn's losing an argument. Let it.
Clover feeds the soil while it's at it. More than you can say for grass.
An oak is a long way to plan ahead. The squirrels plant more of them than people do.
Nothing much grows under a pine. The pine prefers it that way.
Maples sulk if you move them. Pick the spot and keep it.
Boxwood's slow. That isn't a fault. It's a temperament.
Willow will root from a stick pushed into wet ground. Don't tempt it unless you mean it.
You'll want a he and a she for berries. Holly, I mean. It takes two, and you can't tell which is which till it flowers.
Jasmine smells best after dark. So does most of a garden, if you ask me.
Virginia creeper goes red before anything else does. Showing off.
The speckled ones are a little bit delicate by nature. Pretty, though. Give it more light.
A fig, this far north. That's not gardening, that's optimism. I approve.
Your {plant}'s in flower, I hear. Go and look at it properly. Not a glance. Properly.
A pile of old logs is worth more than a flower bed to some. The ones with whiskers, mostly.
Hang a feeder and you'll have chickadees by supper. The jays come after, complaining.
Birds want water more than seed. Shallow, mind. Nobody wants to swim.
Leave a few apples about. Somebody large and polite will come for them.
Leave a pumpkin out after the frost. Somebody always comes for it.
Somebody at your fence is looking for a heap of old leaves. Don't ask me how I know.
Leave the sticks. I know. Leave them anyway.
A puddle's a perfectly good pond if you're small enough.
A nest box, out of the afternoon sun. They're very particular about the afternoon sun.
A warm rock is worth a great deal to something cold-blooded.
Some creatures want a bit of open grass in the sun, with nothing in the way.
Never trust a gentleman with sandy whiskers. Ask any duck.
Squirrels would go to sea if you let them. Very bold about water, for something so small.
Leave your sewing out and a mouse will finish it for you. Never the last buttonhole, though.
Rabbits always find the lettuces. Nobody has ever found out how.
Owls are terribly self-important. Don't ask one a riddle. It won't end well for anyone.
Frogs go fishing, you know. Never catch a thing. Perfectly content about it.
When the peepers start, I open the window. It's the only concert I'll stay up for.
Ducks are dreadful at choosing where to nest. They'll take advice from anyone.
Skunks are perfectly civil if you are.
A possum plays dead because it works. I've done the same at parties.
Keep the apples where the cub can find them and the bins where it can't.
Woodchucks are excellent gardeners. Of my garden, mostly.
Turtles are in no hurry. You could learn from that. I did, eventually.
Luna moths don't eat. Not a bite, their whole lives. I find that very dignified.
Bats are the best neighbours. Out all night, and they never borrow anything.
A chickadee will take seed from your hand if you stand still long enough. Most people can't.
A garter snake in the garden means the garden's doing something right.
If you see the bobcat, you didn't. That's the arrangement.
The coyotes sing on clear nights. Badly, but with feeling.
Porcupines are gentle souls. People just never get close enough to find out.
Otters have more fun than anyone ought to.
That star-nosed fellow is the strangest thing in the county, and the happiest.
Turkeys go about in committees. They never agree on anything either.
Jays have opinions about everything. Usually loudly. Usually wrong.
{pet}'s chipped his pot, I see. Leave it. A pot with a chip has a history.
{pet} likes it here. They all do. It's the compost, I think.
Don't let {pet} near the seedlings. Not out of malice. Just enthusiasm.
You can let them out of the bucket here. Nobody minds.
